Rashi on Berakhot 15a:10:1.hebrew: תרתי ש"מ - כי דרשת נמי שמע בכל לשון שאתה שומע, ש"מ נמי דצריך להשמיע לאזנו:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:10:1.english: Derive two from it - When you also expound "Shema" [to mean] "in any language that you hear," derive from it also that one must make [it] audible to his ear.

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:11:1.hebrew: לא יתרום - לפי שאינו שומע הברכה שהוא מברך עליה:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:11:1.english: He may not separate [terumah] - Because he does not hear the blessing that he recites over it.

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:12:1.hebrew: מאן תנא כו' לא יצא - אפי' בדיעבד. ה"מ כו':
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:12:1.english: Who is the tanna, etc. ... he did not fulfill [his obligation] - [Rabbi Yosei holds that he did not fulfill it] even after the fact. [And the Gemara explains that] this applies only [to the recitation of Shema, etc.].

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:14:1.hebrew: ברכה דרבנן היא - דאמור רבנן (פסחים ד' ז:): כל המצות כולן מברך עליהן עובר לעשייתן:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:14:1.english: The blessing is rabbinic - For the Sages said (Pesachim 7b): "For all the mitzvot, one recites a blessing over them prior to their performance."

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:15:1.hebrew: וממאי דר' יוסי היא - קס"ד: האי דמוקמי לה כר' יוסי, משום דסבירא לן דר' יהודה לכתחלה נמי מכשיר:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:15:1.english: And from where [is it inferred] that it is Rabbi Yosei - It entered [our] mind [to think that] the reason we established it in accordance with Rabbi Yosei [was] because we held that Rabbi Yehuda validates [it] even ab initio.

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:15:2.hebrew: דלמא ר' יהודה היא - וק"ש נמי דיעבד אין, לכתחלה לא. ה"ג, ול"ג אפילו:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:15:2.english: Perhaps it is Rabbi Yehuda - And [regarding] the recitation of Shema as well, after the fact, yes; ab initio, no. This is the reading, and we do not read "even".

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:16:1.hebrew: משום ר' יוסי - להודיעך כחו, דאפי' דיעבד נמי לא יצא:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:16:1.english: Because of Rabbi Yosei - To inform you of his power, that even after the fact he did not fulfill [his obligation].

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:17:1.english: In his heart - That he did not make [it] audible to his ear.

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:18:1.hebrew: ואי ר' יוסי דיעבד נמי לא - דהא בהמ"ז דאורייתא היא: "ואכלת ושבעת וברכת" (דברים ח׳:י׳):
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:18:1.english: And if [it is] Rabbi Yosei, even after the fact [he did] not [fulfill his obligation] - For Grace after Meals is from the Torah, [as it is written:] "And you shall eat and be satisfied, and bless" (Deuteronomy 8:10).

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:19:1.hebrew: אלא מאי ר' יהודה - וק"ש דיעבד אין, לכתחלה לא; והא דתרומה וברכת המזון — דר' יהודה:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:19:1.english: Rather, what [is it]? Rabbi Yehuda - And [regarding] the recitation of Shema, after the fact, yes; ab initio, no; and that [Mishnah] concerning terumah and [the baraita concerning] Grace after Meals are [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:1:1.english: He should relieve himself - For his bodily needs.

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:22:1.hebrew: אלא רבי יהודה לכתחלה קאמר - והא דרבי יהודה בריה דר' שמעון בן פזי — ר' יהודה היא; ודתרומה — ר' יוסי היא, ומודה הוא דברכות דרבנן, דיעבד שפיר דמי; והא דברכת המזון — ר' יהודה היא משמיה דרביה ר' אלעזר בן עזריה, דאומר: "צריך שישמיע לאזנו", וכל "צריך" לכתחלה משמע, הא דיעבד שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:22:1.english: Rather, Rabbi Yehuda says [even] ab initio - And that [baraita taught by] Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda; and that [Mishnah] concerning terumah is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yosei, and he concedes that [since] blessings are Rabbinic, after the fact [it] is acceptable; and that [baraita] concerning Grace after Meals is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda in the name of his teacher, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, who says: "One must make [it] audible to his ear," and every [use of] "must" implies ab initio, whereas after the fact, [it] is acceptable.

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:22:2.hebrew: אחר כוונת הלב כו' - ואפי' לכתחלה נמי א"צ:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:22:2.english: [The words] follow the intention of the heart, etc. - And even ab initio, one also does not need [to make it audible to his ear].

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:23:1.hebrew: השתא דאתית להכי - דאשמעת לן פלוגתא דר"מ:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:23:1.english: Now that you have arrived at this - That you have informed us of the dispute of Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:23:2.hebrew: אפילו תימא ר' יהודה - דאמר בק"ש נמי יצא, דיעבד — אין, לכתחלה — לא. והא דברכת המזון ודתרומה — רבי יהודה היא. ודקא קשיא לך: דר' יהודה בריה דר"ש בן פזי מני? ר"מ היא, דמכשר לכתחלה:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:23:2.english: Even if you say Rabbi Yehuda - That he says [that] regarding the recitation of Shema as well, 'he has fulfilled [his obligation]' [means]: after the fact, yes; ab initio, no. And that [baraita] of Grace after Meals and that [mishna] of terumah are [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda. And as for that which posed a difficulty to you, 'Whose [opinion] is [the baraita taught by] Rabbi Yehuda the son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi?' — it is Rabbi Meir, who validates [it] ab initio.

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:25:1.hebrew: מאן תנא חרש דיעבד נמי לא - דקתני גבי שוטה:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:25:1.english: Who is the tanna [who holds that regarding] a deaf person, even after the fact, [it is] also not [valid] - For it is taught alongside an imbecile [who is disqualified even after the fact].

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:25:2.english: He did not fulfill [his obligation] - This is after the fact.

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:2:1.hebrew: דכתיב ארחץ בנקיון - משמע: ארחץ כל הגוף, ולא כתיב ארחיץ. כפי לדרשה אתא — לומר שמעלה עליו שכר רחיצת כפיו כאלו טבל כל גופו:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:2:1.english: As it is written: "I will wash in purity" - [The word] "I will wash" implies [washing] the entire body, and it is not written "I will wash" [*arḥitz*]. [The word] "my hands" comes for an exposition — to say that [Scripture] credits him with the reward for washing his hands as if he had immersed his entire body.

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:5:1.hebrew: לק"ש - בעידנא דק"ש, שזמנה קבוע, פן יעבור הזמן. אבל לתפלה, דכל היום זמנה, הוא צריך למהדר אמיא:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:5:1.english: For the recitation of the Shema - [This applies] at the time of the recitation of the Shema, whose time is fixed, lest the time pass. But for prayer, whose time is the entire day, he must go out of his way to seek water.

Rashi on Berakhot 15a:7:1.hebrew: ולא דקדק באותיותיה - לפרשן יפה בשפתיו:
Rashi on Berakhot 15a:7:1.english: And was not precise in its letters - To enunciate them clearly with his lips.

Tosafot on Berakhot 15a:15:1.hebrew: דילמא ר' יהודה היא - וא"ת: והלא אין נזכר ר' יהודה ברישא? וי"ל: דפשיטא, מדסיפא ר' יהודה — רישא נמי ר' יהודה, ופליגי במילתא דר' יהודה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 15a:15:1.english: Perhaps it is Rabbi Yehuda - And if you say: But behold, Rabbi Yehuda is not mentioned in the first clause [of the Mishnah]? And one can answer that it is obvious: since in the latter clause [it is] Rabbi Yehuda, in the first clause [it is] also Rabbi Yehuda, and they disagree over the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

Tosafot on Berakhot 15a:16:1.hebrew: להודיעך כחו דרבי יוסי - וא"ת: לשמעינן כחו דרבי יהודה, דכח דהתירא עדיף. וי"ל: כיון דרבי יהודה לא דריש "השמע לאזנך", אין כאן שום חדוש, ופשיטא דלכתחלה; ומהיכא תיתי לאוסרו? אי שרי דיעבד — הוא הדין לכתחלה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 15a:16:1.english: "To inform you of the power of Rabbi Yosei" - And if you will say: Let [the Mishnah] teach us the power of Rabbi Yehuda, as the power of permitting is preferred! And it may be answered: Since Rabbi Yehuda does not expound "make it audible to your ear," there is no novelty here, and it is obvious that [it is permitted] ab initio; for from where would it be derived to forbid it? If it is permitted after the fact, the same applies ab initio.

Tosafot on Berakhot 15a:18:1.hebrew: אי ר' יוסי דיעבד נמי לא - וא"ת: לעולם אימא לך רבי יוסי היא, וברכת המזון שאני, דלא כתיב ביה "שמע"; דבשלמא תרומה דלעיל ומגילה דלקמן, שהן מדרבנן — יש לדמותם לק"ש, שתקנו שצריך שישמיע לאזנו כמו בק"ש, ותקנו ממש שלא יצא כמו בק"ש; אבל בבהמ"ז, שהיא מדאורייתא, כיון דלא כתיב ביה "שמע" — למה יש לנו לתקן שלא יצא אם לא השמיע לאזנו, כיון דמה"ת יצא? וי"ל: כיון שתקנו שצריך להשמיע לאזנו כמו בק"ש, הואיל ומדרבנן מיהא צריך להשמיע — אין לחלק בין ק"ש ובין בהמ"ז, דאפילו בדיעבד אית לן למימר שלא יצא:
Tosafot on Berakhot 15a:18:1.english: If [it is] Rabbi Yosei, even after the fact [he did] not [fulfill his obligation] - And if you say: Actually, I could say to you [that] it is Rabbi Yosei, and Grace after Meals is different, as "Hear" is not written regarding it. For it is well [regarding] terumah above and Megillah below, which are Rabbinic, [that] one can compare them to [the recitation of] Shema, [in] that they enacted that one must make [it] audible to his ear just as in [the recitation of] Shema, and they actually enacted that he does not fulfill [his obligation], just as in [the recitation of] Shema. However, regarding Grace after Meals, which is from the Torah, since "Hear" is not written regarding it, why should we enact that he did not fulfill [his obligation] if he did not make [it] audible to his ear, since by Torah law he fulfilled [it]? And one can answer: Since they enacted that one must make [it] audible to his ear just as in [the recitation of] Shema, since at any rate Rabbinically he must make [it] audible, we do not distinguish between [the recitation of] Shema and Grace after Meals, so that even after the fact, we must say that he did not fulfill [his obligation].

Tosafot on Berakhot 15a:25:1.hebrew: ורבי יהודה מכשיר בקטן - וא"ת: באיזה קטן מיירי? אי בקטן שלא הגיע לחנוך — הא אמרינן בפרק ראוהו בית דין (ר"ה ד' כט.) שכל שאינו מחוייב בדבר אינו מוציא את הרבים, ומ"ט דר' יהודה דמכשיר? ואי בהגיע לחנוך — מאי טעמייהו דרבנן דאסרי? הרי קריאת מגילה דרבנן, ואמרי' קטן שהגיע לחנוך מדרבנן כגדול ופוטר דרבנן, כדאמר לקמן בפ' מי שמתו (ברכות ד' כ:) דקטן מוציא אביו שלא אכל אלא כזית, דהיינו דרבנן. וי"ל: שאני ברכת המזון, שהיא חומרא יתירתא יותר מדאורייתא, ובקל נפטרים ממנה, כדאמרי' לקמן (שם): והם החמירו על עצמם או בכזית או בכביצה. א"נ: התם ליכא בקטן אלא חד דרבנן, דמיירי שהקטן אכל כדי שביעה — לכך אתי דרבנן ומוציא דרבנן; אבל הכא, דגבי קטן איכא תרתי דרבנן — דהמגילה דרבנן והקטן דרבנן — אינו יכול להוציא היכא דליכא אלא חד דרבנן:
Tosafot on Berakhot 15a:25:1.english: "And Rabbi Yehuda deems a minor fit" - And if you say: With what [kind of] minor are we dealing? If [it is] with a minor who has not reached [the age of] training [in mitzvot] — behold, we say in the chapter [entitled] Ra'ahu Beit Din (Rosh Hashanah 29a) that anyone who is not obligated in a matter cannot fulfill the obligation of the many [on their behalf], and what is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda who deems [him] fit? And if [it is] with [a minor who has] reached [the age of] training — what is the reasoning of the Rabbis who forbid [him]? Behold, reading the Megillah is rabbinic, and we say that a minor who has reached [the age of] training is rabbinically like an adult and exempts [another whose obligation is] rabbinic, as [the Gemara] says later in the chapter [entitled] Mi SheMeito (Berakhot 20b), that a minor fulfills [the obligation of] his father who ate only an olive-bulk, which is rabbinic. And one can say: Grace after Meals is different, for it is an extra stringency beyond Torah law, and one is easily exempted from it, as [the Gemara] says later (ibid.): "And they were stringent with themselves [to recite it for] either an olive-bulk or an egg-bulk." Alternatively, there, regarding the minor, there is only a single rabbinic [factor], for we are dealing with [a case where] the minor ate to satiety; therefore, [one with] a rabbinic [obligation] comes and fulfills [the obligation of one with] a rabbinic [obligation]. But here, regarding the minor, there are two rabbinic [factors] — for the Megillah [obligation] is rabbinic and the minor [being obligated] is rabbinic — [so] he cannot fulfill [the obligation of another] where there is only a single rabbinic [factor].

Tosafot on Berakhot 15a:4:1.hebrew: אמאן דמהדר אמיא בעידן ק"ש - ויש ספרים דגרסי: "הני מילי לק"ש, אבל לתפלה לא", דקאמר רשב"ל (פסחים מו.): "לגבל ולתפלה ד' מילין". ונראה דלא גרסינן ליה, דהוא הדין לענין צלותא נמי מטעם שלא יעבור זמן תפלה — דמאי שנא ק"ש מתפלה? וגם יש לקמן פרק מי שמתו (ברכות ד' כב.): "בטלוה לנטילותא כדרב חסדא, דלייט אמאן דמהדר אמיא בעידן צלותא"; ומדלא הזכיר שם ק"ש, משמע דבכל ענין מותר. וההיא דרשב"ל דאמר "ולתפלה ד' מילין", פירש רש"י: להתפלל שם במנין:
Tosafot on Berakhot 15a:4:1.english: "[Rav Ḥisda curses] one who seeks water at the time of the recitation of Shema" - And there are books that have the reading: "This applies [only] to the recitation of Shema, but for prayer, [it is] not [so]," as Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said (Pesachim 46a): "For kneading and for prayer, four mil." And it appears that we should not have this reading, for the same applies regarding prayer as well, on account of [the concern] that the time for prayer might pass — for what is the difference between the recitation of Shema and prayer? And it also states later in chapter Mi Shemeito (Berakhot 22a): "They abolished washing [of the hands], in accordance with Rav Ḥisda, who cursed one who seeks water at the time of prayer"; and since it did not mention the recitation of Shema there, it implies that in every case it is permitted. And as for that [statement] of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish who said, "And for prayer, four mil" — Rashi explained: to pray there with a quorum [minyan].
